messages:
alice: Heads-up — nightly evals started spamming duplicate GHA runs tonight, lots of runner timeouts around 23:00 UTC. Anyone else seeing it?

ben: Yup saw that. Looks like cron jitter + the new per-model matrix are overlapping. GH cancels not always firing, so multiple shards queue and exhaust hosted runners.

carlos: Logs attached from one failed run:```
2026-03-19T23:01:12Z runner: starting job eval/nightly-shard-3
2026-03-19T23:01:13Z queue: no free runners, waiting...
2026-03-19T23:05:01Z error: waiting for a free runner
2026-03-19T23:10:00Z timeout: job exceeded 30m
```

diana: We should add GH Actions concurrency with `cancel-in-progress: true` per-model group and also spread cron times. Example snippet: ```yaml
concurrency:
  group: eval-${{ matrix.model }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

ben: Also add minute offsets to the schedule so model A runs at 00, model B at 05, etc. small script to compute offsets from model name/sha works fine. one-liner I use: `python -c "import hashlib,sys;print(int(hashlib.sha1(sys.argv[1].encode()).hexdigest(),16)%60)" MODELNAME`

alice: Seeing `error: waiting for a free runner` repeatedly. Buildkite jobs unaffected — maybe move heavy evals to dedicated Buildkite nightly workers while we stabilize GHA?

infra-bot: Created ticket <https://redwood.internal/INFRA-312> to track CI runner saturation and schedule jitter. Assigned infra oncall.

eval-bot: Eval summary: 6 failed runs, 4 cancelled, median runtime increased from 18m to 32m vs last night. Key failure = runner throttling / timeouts.

diana: I can open a quick PR to add `concurrency` + cron offsets + `cancel-in-progress`. Also add `if: always()` to ensure cleanup. Should I proceed?

ben: sgtm. Add a tiny retry on transient failures (2 retries) and a short randomized sleep before heavy shards start to further desync.

alice: Assign to @diana and put note in PR title: "gha-eval-schedule-jitter-mitigation". After merge, run a focused smoke job nightly for three nights. :thumbsup:

carlos: I'll watch logs and page if failure rate > 10% for two consecutive nights.

alice: Thanks all. Keeping this thread for updates. If anyone notices other flakiness, drop it here or tag infra oncall. :eyes:
